title: Word boundaries
text: I came across an interesting article.
tip: Focus on how “came across an” runs together in connected speech.

title: Weak forms
text: We need to deal with the problem today.
tip: In fast speech, “to” may be reduced to a weak /tə/ sound.

title: Fluent linking
text: I finally got around to fixing the door.
tip: Notice how vowel and consonant transitions blend across word boundaries.

title: Contractions
text: That’s the point. If the task feels manageable, I’m much more likely to follow through on it.
tip: Listen for contracted “that is” and “I am”.

title: Stress shifts
text: The results bear out our initial theory.
tip: Notice the emphasis on content words: results, bear out, theory.

title: Reduced vowels
text: The signal was intriguing, but an ordinary technical source had not been ruled out.
tip: Unstressed syllables commonly use reduced vowels in American English.

title: Numbers and amounts
text: The renovation cost twenty seven thousand four hundred dollars.
tip: Write the amount in words to practice number recognition.

title: Time and dates
text: The meeting begins at a quarter past eight on November fifth.
tip: Listen for the time expression and the ordinal date.

title: Uncertain claims
text: The evidence was incomplete, so I’m reluctant to draw a conclusion.
tip: Reluctant signals hesitation rather than certainty.

title: Implied contrast
text: The plan looked promising; however, the funding was insufficient.
tip: However signals contrast between expectations and outcome.

title: Fast spoken sequence
text: We’re going to narrow down the options before lunch.
tip: Notice “we’re” and “going to” in natural speech.

title: A subtle correction
text: I didn’t say it was impossible; I said it was unlikely.
tip: Stress changes the intended meaning of the correction.

title: The exception matters
text: The report was thorough, yet it overlooked one crucial assumption.
tip: The contrast word yet shifts the conclusion; note which part of the review was incomplete.

title: An estimate is not a promise
text: The package should arrive by Thursday, although the delivery date is not guaranteed.
tip: Should and not guaranteed express uncertainty rather than a firm promise.

title: Price and cents
text: The replacement part costs one hundred forty three dollars and sixty five cents.
tip: Listen for the difference between dollar amounts and cents.

title: A gate change
text: Flight two hundred eighteen now departs from gate thirty four at nine twenty five.
tip: Record the flight number, the gate number, and the time separately.

title: Missing consonants
text: We asked the staff to check the last train before we left.
tip: Notice how word boundaries can be harder to hear when neighboring consonants meet.

title: Linking across words
text: She came across an old article about the abandoned train station.
tip: Listen for across an: a consonant links to the following unstressed vowel.

title: Weak forms in a request
text: Could you send her a copy of the final report before lunch?
tip: Unstressed pronouns and function words may be reduced in casual American speech.

title: Negative contraction
text: I wouldn't rule out a second explanation until we review the evidence.
tip: A negative contraction changes the meaning; do not confuse would with would not.

title: Two valid options
text: We can either postpone the launch or reduce the scope, but we cannot do both.
tip: Pay attention to either, or, and cannot do both.

title: Order of events
text: After the meeting, she went back to the office and followed up on the complaint.
tip: The sequence markers after and and identify the order of events.

title: Compare two numbers
text: The first estimate was eighteen percent, whereas the final figure was thirteen percent.
tip: Write both percentages in the order spoken; whereas marks a contrast.

title: A conditional plan
text: Unless the weather improves by Friday, the outdoor event will be called off.
tip: Unless introduces a condition; identify what must change to avoid cancellation.
